title: E-Signature Tools for HubSpot: QuickSigner, DocuSign, Dropbox Sign, and HubSpot Quotes — Jon Martin
seoTitle: E-Signature Tools for HubSpot (Quotes, DocuSign, Dropbox Sign)
description: HubSpot quote e-sign compared with DocuSign, Dropbox Sign, and QuickSigner: plans, prices, and which ones actually connect to HubSpot. Checked Nov 23, 2026.
dek: First ask whether HubSpot's own quote e-sign already covers the job. Then pick a native CRM integration, or a cheaper tool you are willing to wire up.
Four options lined up for HubSpot teams: HubSpot quotes, DocuSign, Dropbox Sign, and QuickSigner.

Best for.docusign: Teams already on DocuSign that want envelopes created from HubSpot records.
Best for.dropbox-sign: Teams that want signature requests from contact, company, or deal records, with the signed file saved back.
Best for.quicksigner: A low published price and unlimited documents, if someone can build an API connection.

Plan or seat needed.quicksigner: The eSignature API sits on the Professional plan.

sections.label: Start with HubSpot's own quote e-sign

blocks.html: Before you add a signer, check whether {{link:hubspot}} already covers it. HubSpot can collect e-signatures on quotes, and {{fact:hubspot.esign_dropbox}}.

On the current quoting tools, {{fact:hubspot.esign_revenue}}. HubSpot's own examples: {{fact:hubspot.esign_rev_pro}}, and {{fact:hubspot.esign_rev_ent}}. If you need more, the catalog lists an {{fact:hubspot.esign_addon}}.

Revenue Hub seat list prices are {{fact:hubspot.revenue_seat_pro}} and {{fact:hubspot.revenue_seat_ent}}. That is the price of the hub, not of e-sign on its own, because e-sign is a feature of the hub.

One warning for anyone reading older guides: {{fact:hubspot.legacy_quotes}}. {{fact:hubspot.legacy_esign}}. So do not tell a new customer to plan around legacy quotes, and reconcile the two official articles before you rely on a Starter answer.
If the team signs sales quotes inside HubSpot and already has, or will buy, Revenue Hub, start with the native quote e-sign. Add a specialist when you need to sign documents that are not quotes.

items: Already have DocuSign and want envelopes from HubSpot records: DocuSign.
Want signature requests from contact, company, or deal records, saved back: Dropbox Sign.
Want the lowest published price and can own an API build: QuickSigner.

blocks.html: QuickSigner has an affiliate link and the others do not. That is not a reason to rank it ahead of the native HubSpot options. It is the cheap choice that takes developer time.

If you build the connection, {{fact:quicksigner.api}}. Do not confuse QuickSigner with the Swedish product QuickSign at quicksign.se. Deeper write-up: QuickSigner.

items: Quotes already in HubSpot, and you have or will buy Revenue Hub: start with the native quote e-sign.
Contracts from contact, company, or deal records, and you want a native app: DocuSign or Dropbox Sign.
Lowest published price, and someone can own an API build: QuickSigner.
Whatever you pick, confirm who signs, what saves back to the record, and who administers it before you roll it out.

faq.q: How many e-signatures does HubSpot include?
faq.a: HubSpot's examples: {{fact:hubspot.esign_rev_pro}}, and {{fact:hubspot.esign_rev_ent}}. The catalog lists an {{fact:hubspot.esign_addon}}.

faq.q: Does Dropbox Sign integrate with HubSpot?
Should a HubSpot team start with QuickSigner?
faq.a: Only if they need a low published price and can own an API connection. If they mainly sign HubSpot quotes, start with HubSpot's own e-sign. For a native button on records, look at DocuSign or Dropbox Sign first.

closing: Check whether HubSpot already signs the document before you pay for another signer.
